lens: Second-round independent recruiter workflow review of evaluation-platform gating, workflow evidence requirements, typed review boundaries, Opik score semantics, and release-readiness honesty.

findings.criterion: Engineering completeness and release-readiness absence should stay distinguishable in the authoritative local gate, not only in proof summaries.
findings.observation: The repository now separates deterministic safety from release readiness in the PRD, CLI summary, and final proof, but the authoritative gate still applies one global missing human-workflow requirement to every scored capability. In the final TS-TRJ-005 local artifact, decision, scenario, and trajectory all become needs_review even though every deterministic score passed. That means a consumer reading only the authoritative gate still has to rely on higher-level summaries to learn that the blocker is missing human evidence rather than a deterministic safety failure.
findings.evidence: packages/evaluation/src/gates.ts:52-63 and 108-133 return needs_review for any capability when globallyMissingEvaluatorIds is non-empty and then assign that global list to every capability; apps/eval-runner/src/cli.ts:281-306 adds a separate deterministicSafetySummary only after the gate is computed; docs/evaluations/2026-09-01-evaluation-platform/opik-final-v2/runs/evaluation_run_a52942251e74a9551f8f99efe43c61e1/run-artifact.22fdabb789ab24ab78f11f0ccfc33ac4637b29ea21e7fb78a20e281b6e14bb8d.json:1 shows decision, scenario, and trajectory each with missingEvaluatorIds ["human-workflow"] while every recorded deterministic score status is "pass"; docs/evaluations/2026-09-01-evaluation-platform/README.md:11-15 and docs/evaluations/2026-09-01-evaluation-platform/opik-integration-proof.json:134-140 explain the distinction only at the summary layer.
findings.user_impact: A recruiter-audit or release consumer that trusts the local gate artifact as authority can still misread a fully passing deterministic replay as a uniform workflow failure across all capabilities. That weakens the clarity of the exact artifact intended to support release adjudication.
findings.recommendation: Keep missing required human evidence as a release-readiness block, but encode it in a machine-readable layer that does not overwrite deterministic-only capability passes inside the authoritative gate artifact. A falsifiable fix is: on a P0 replay with no human-workflow scores, release readiness remains needs_review, yet any capability whose bound deterministic criteria all pass and whose scenario binding does not require a human score for that capability can still remain pass in the local gate.
findings.verification: Re-run pnpm eval:proof and inspect the emitted local gate JSON for a P0 replay. The proof should still report releaseReadinessNeedsReviewCount 12, while at least one deterministic-only capability in the authoritative gate artifact remains pass instead of inheriting global missingEvaluatorIds.

strengths: All 12 current P0 scenarios now require human-workflow for gate authority, while the full suite still validates as 36 scenarios with 12 P0, 6 dev, 8 held_out, 10 red_team, and zero contamination findings; confirmed by pnpm eval:validate and by P0 scenario bindings such as evals/v2/scenarios/ts-act-102.r1.json:36-63, evals/v2/scenarios/ts-cap-005.r1.json:36-62, and evals/v2/scenarios/ts-id-103.r1.json:36-60.

The default runner honestly leaves release readiness at needs_review when required human evidence is absent: apps/eval-runner/src/runSuite.ts:237-245 only executes deterministic evaluators by default, packages/evaluation/src/gates.ts:108-133 converts missing required evaluator bindings into missing_required_evaluator, and docs/evaluations/2026-09-01-evaluation-platform/opik-integration-proof.json:134-140 records 12 deterministic-safety passes with 12 release-readiness needs_review results.

Typed review-boundary separation is now explicit and enforced end to end: apps/eval-runner/src/contracts.ts:46-62 requires reviewBoundary on every observation, apps/eval-runner/src/reviewBoundary.ts:22-35 and 43-167 type and validate evidence, confirmedState, interpretations, proposedActions, and observedOutcomes, and apps/eval-runner/src/builtinExecutors.ts:406-455 plus 553-597 require the same separation for control-plane and remote responses.

Opik score projection no longer flattens atomic criterion evidence into an aggregate approval signal: apps/eval-runner/src/contracts.ts:141-156 defines semantic atomic_criterion with aggregateApproval false, apps/eval-runner/src/safeExportPolicy.ts:192-245 preserves gateAuthority, veto, and evidenceLocators in the safe score, apps/eval-runner/src/opik/opikTransport.ts:367-403 writes that metadata onto each projected score span, and docs/evaluations/2026-09-01-evaluation-platform/opik-integration-proof.json:122-132 asserts atomic non-aggregate score semantics.
missing_evidence: The repository still does not include named recruiter field evidence or versioned atomic human gold showing that the proposals reduce recruiter correction burden or improve momentum in real workflow conditions; docs/evaluations/2026-09-01-evaluation-platform/README.md:32-35 explicitly preserves that absence instead of overstating readiness.

The 36-case synthetic suite covers key recruiter failure modes such as no_action, clarification, wrong-person ambiguity, wrong-speaker attribution, and retry recovery through scenarios including evals/v2/scenarios/ts-act-107.r1.json:6-8, evals/v2/scenarios/ts-act-102.r1.json:6-7, evals/v2/scenarios/ts-id-103.r1.json:6-7, evals/v2/scenarios/ts-cap-005.r1.json:6-7, and evals/v2/scenarios/ts-trj-006.r1.json:6-7, but synthetic coverage is not the same as evidence that independent recruiters would trust and adopt the workflow under interruption-heavy real usage.
open_questions: Which single local artifact should future release automation consume as authority once deterministic safety and release readiness are fully separated: the gate JSON itself, or a new release-semantics artifact derived from but not overwriting the gate?
